title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: A dart board is a regular octagon divided into regions as shown. Suppose that a dart thrown at the board is equally likely to land anywhere on the board. What is the probability that the dart lands within the center square?

solutions.text:
Assume the octagon has edge length \(1.\) The four corner triangles are right isosceles with legs \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\) and area \(\dfrac14\) each. The four rectangles are \(1\) by \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\) with area \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\) each, and the center square has area \(1.\)

The total area is \[ 4\cdot\dfrac14+4\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}+1=2+2\sqrt2. \] The probability of hitting the center square is \[ \dfrac{1}{2+2\sqrt2}=\dfrac{\sqrt2-1}{2}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Set the octagon’s edge to \(1\) and split it into the center square, four rectangles, and four corner triangles
The corner triangles are right isosceles with legs \(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\)
